Rubric (no matter numbers in titles): 1006-00008 (Crestline Packaging bolt-on, APA June 16, 2025, closed Aug. 15, 2025) and its disclosure-schedules.docx, plus a precision criterion allowing only that matter.

runs.failure_point: The deal it needed was in its own disclosure-file search results, but it ranked candidates by matter number, opened only high-numbered matters and named an older deal.

first_error.why: Its disclosure-file glob listed the matter's schedules (it even named the matter in its summary), but it chose what to list by highest matter number instead of by date and never opened that matter.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) the search review called ranking by matter number only an assumption; the write review asked to check other candidates' dates.

runs.failure_point: It named the right deal and its schedules, but its comparison table presented several other matters as closed deals with disclosure schedules.

first_error.why: Alongside the chosen deal, the answer describes five other matters it read at [29]-[68] as closed M&A deals with disclosure schedules, which the request's single-deal answer does not allow.

divergence: Mixed outcomes, all failing. All three runs surfaced the matter's disclosure-schedules file in store-wide searches. T0 and T1 then ranked candidates by matter number, listed and read only the highest-numbered deal matters, and named older deals (surfaced, never opened); in both runs the critic said matter-number order is only an assumption and asked for dates, and the agent kept checking higher-numbered matters. T2 took its candidates from a content scan whose hits started low in the number range, read the schedules and closing records of seven matters, compared closing dates and named the right deal (2/3), but its answer also described several other matters as closed deals with schedules, which failed precision; the critic did not name that.
